values: Using non-production data, open All new public, member, and administrator product surfaces. Prepare the state named “External-link indication”, perform the single relevant navigation or action, and record the visible result, resulting URL, HTTP status where applicable, and browser console/network errors.
At “External-link indication”, content remains readable with no clipping or horizontal overflow; focus, labels, status meaning, touch targets, and motion behavior remain perceivable and operable.
Visitor, keyboard user, screen-reader user, or administrator
Use staging data for populated, empty, locked, loading, error, and confirmation states; reduced motion available. Use synthetic records and do not change production data.
Open /project/create; reach Terms and visibility; inspect the application access control.
Control is visible, defaults to Active GO members only, and explains that free users can apply only when all signed-in users are allowed.
Create or edit a project; choose All signed-in users, including free users; save; refresh the project and edit form.
The broader application policy saves and remains selected after refresh; the project detail copy reflects the setting.
Hiring project owned by the test account
As a signed-in free user, open a hiring project configured for all signed-in users and submit an application.
Application is created successfully once; no paid membership prompt blocks the flow.
Free user applies to opted-in project
Free account; public hiring project with applicationAccess set to all_signed_in_users
As a paid member, apply to one members-only project and one all-signed-in-users project.
Both applications are accepted under their respective policies.
Paid member applies under both policies
Active Community or Business account; two hiring projects with different policies
As a project admin who is not the creator, open the edit form and attempt to change who may apply; also attempt the direct update request.
The control is read-only and the direct update is rejected; other permitted project edits remain unaffected.
Project admin cannot change application policy
Admin access to another user's project; separate API request capability
Open an older project with no applicationAccess value; inspect its detail page and attempt application as a free user.
The project displays and enforces Active GO members only, preserving legacy behavior.
Legacy hiring project without applicationAccess field
As an anonymous visitor, open a hiring project configured for all signed-in users and click Apply.
Visitor is prompted to sign in; no application is created before authentication.
Public hiring project with all-signed-in-users policy
Attempt to apply to private, invite-only, or non-hiring projects under both application policies.
Visibility and hiring-status rules still reject the application regardless of the selected applicant policy.
Application policy does not bypass project access rules
Test projects covering private/invite-only and non-hiring states
Send direct application requests as a free user to members-only and all-signed-in-users projects; send an unauthorized policy update as a non-owner admin.
The server enforces the stored policy and rejects the unauthorized policy update; UI restrictions cannot be bypassed through the API.
Authenticated test tokens; projects with both policies
Change a project from members-only to all-signed-in-users and inspect an existing application before and after the change.
Existing application status and applicant data are unchanged; the new policy applies only to future applications.
Project with an existing application and creator access
